newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK jobless drops to six-year low in Dec. [CORRECTED 23:03 GMT]
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK jobless drops to six-year low in Dec. [CORRECTED 23:03 GMT]

text.p: British unemployment fell to a six-year low of 1.88 million in December and the jobless rate dipped to 6.7 percent, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said on Wednesday.

The larger than expected seasonally adjusted fall of 45,100 in the jobless register reflected robust economic activity, but steady growth in November average earnings showed this is still not being reflected in rising wage costs.
The figures were welcomed by the Conservative government, which is anxious to highlight any good economic news to improve its prospects in the forthcoming election, due by May.

"Unemployment is falling right across the country and the smile on Britain's face can broaden," Prime Minister John Major said. "In the last four years, Britain has created more jobs than all the other major countries of Europe put together.
The ONS said the number of people in employment (corrects)
stood at 26.076 million at the end of the third quarter, a rise of 299,000 compared with a year earlier.
In a swipe at the opposition Labour party, which has a strong lead in opinion polls, Major said:

"People will have to choose if they want to stick with the successful policies that are bringing stability and prosperity, or are willing to risk the rewards of hard work by voting for an inexperienced, unknown alternative."

Labour, which accuses the government of manipulating the statistics, said the official numbers were "figures of fantasy." Labour employment spokesman Ian McCartney said figures from the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development showed that in 18.9 percent of British households, no-one of working age had a job.
"The only growth industry in Britain under the Tories is job insecurity, with half of those actually finding jobs likely to be unemployed again in less than a year," he said.
The ONS said underlying average earnings rose four percent in the year to November, the same rate as in the previous month.
Unit wage costs were up 4.2 percent in the three months to November compared with a year earlier.
The ONS said special factors had inflated the drop in unemployment in December, which followed a dramatic 95,400 fall in November.

The introduction of a new jobseekers' allowance, under which people receive unemployment benefit only if they can prove they are actively seeking work, may have accounted for up to 10,000 of the fall in December.

City economists said the figures were unlikely to have much impact on the debate between the government and the Bank of England over whether interest rates need to be increased to prevent a resurgence in inflation.
Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke was meeting Bank of England Governor Eddie George on Wednesday afternoon for their monthly meeting on monetary policy.

The central bank has been pressing for higher rates but economists said an unexpected drop in manufacturing output last month, softer than expected Christmas retail sales and Wednesday's steady earnings figures would give Clarke ammunition to resist a rate rise.
Governments are reluctant to raise interest rates in the run-up to an election as this means dearer mortgages for millions of home-owners with variable-rate loans.
